assignment.title: Algebra II Honors — Lesson 2 Day 1: Parent Functions and Key Attributes

questions.prompt: Use the graph of f(x) = |x|. State the domain and range.
Use the graph of f(x) = x². State where the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.
For f(x)=2x+1, identify the domain and range.

optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): Any real number can be doubled and increased by 1, so every x is allowed.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): Every real input works, including 0 and negatives: f(0) = 1.

optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): A line with a nonzero slope keeps rising, so it reaches every real output.
optionRationales.[1, ∞): 1 is the y-intercept, not a lowest value; the line keeps going down to the left: f(−3) = −5.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): Outputs can be 0 or negative: f(−3) = −5.

questions.prompt: Analyze the parent function f(x)=|x|. State the domain, range, vertex, and minimum point.
Analyze the parent function f(x)=√x. State the domain, range, x-intercept, and y-intercept.
Analyze the parent function f(x)=x³. State the domain, range, and where it is increasing.
Analyze the parent function f(x)=∛x. State the domain, range, and where it is increasing.
Analyze the reciprocal parent function f(x)=1/x. State the domain, range, where it is positive, and where it is negative.
Analyze the exponential parent function f(x)=2ˣ. State the domain, range, y-intercept, and where it is increasing.
Analyze the logarithmic parent function f(x)=log₂(x). State the domain, range, x-intercept, and where it is increasing.
Connect each parent function to its asymptotic behavior.

optionRationales.vertical x=0 and horizontal y=0: 1/x is undefined at x = 0, and its outputs shrink toward 0 as x grows in either direction.
optionRationales.horizontal y=1 only: 1/x never settles near 1, and its break at x = 0 is an asymptote too.
optionRationales.no asymptotes: Dividing by x fails at x = 0, so the graph breaks there, and far out it flattens toward a line.

optionRationales.horizontal y=0: As x goes left, 2ˣ gets closer and closer to 0 without reaching it.
optionRationales.vertical x=0: 2ˣ is defined at x = 0 (2⁰ = 1), so there is no break there.
optionRationales.no asymptotes: To the left, 2ˣ keeps shrinking toward a value it never reaches, and that line is an asymptote.

optionRationales.vertical x=0: log₂(x) is defined only for x > 0, and it drops without bound as x nears 0.
optionRationales.horizontal y=0: y = 0 belongs to 2ˣ; log₂(x) is its inverse, so x and y trade roles.
optionRationales.no asymptotes: log₂(x) is not defined at 0 or below, and near 0 it drops without bound, which is an asymptote.

questions.prompt: Identify the family and key attributes of f(x)=√x.

optionRationales.square root: √x takes the principal square root of x: the square root parent function.
optionRationales.cube root: A cube root carries a small 3 on its radical, as in ∛x; this radical has none.
optionRationales.absolute value: Absolute value is |x|; this function takes a root.
optionRationales.reciprocal: The reciprocal is 1/x; this function takes a root, not 1 divided by x.

optionRationales.[0, ∞): A real square root needs a number that is not negative, and √0 = 0 is defined, so x starts at 0.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): Negative numbers have no real square root, so not every x is allowed.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): x = 0 works, since √0 = 0, so 0 belongs in the domain.

optionRationales.[0, ∞): √x gives the root that is not negative, starting at √0 = 0, so the outputs are 0 and up.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): √x always gives the root that is not negative, so outputs below 0 never appear.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): The output 0 happens at x = 0, so it belongs in the range.

questions.prompt: Identify the family and key attributes of f(x)=1/x.

optionRationales.reciprocal: 1/x divides 1 by x: the reciprocal parent function.
optionRationales.exponential: Exponential functions have x in the exponent, like 2ˣ; here x is in the denominator.
optionRationales.logarithmic: A logarithm is written log(x); here 1 is divided by x.
optionRationales.cubic: Cubic is x³; here x is in the denominator, not raised to the third power.

optionRationales.(−∞, 0) ∪ (0, ∞): You can divide 1 by any number except 0, so x can be any real number but 0.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): Dividing by 0 is undefined, so x = 0 has to be left out.
optionRationales.(0, ∞): Negative inputs work: 1/(−2) = −1/2; only 0 is left out.

optionRationales.(−∞, 0) ∪ (0, ∞): 1/x can be any nonzero number, but 1 divided by a number is never 0.
optionRationales.(−∞, ∞): 1 divided by any number is never 0, so 0 is missing from the outputs.
optionRationales.[0, ∞): Negative inputs give negative outputs, and 1/x never equals 0.

questions.prompt: Use the graph of f(x)=−√x. State the domain, range, and whether the function is increasing or decreasing.
Use the graph of f(x)=(1/2)ˣ. State the domain, range, and whether the function is increasing or decreasing.
Use the graph of f(x)=log₁⁄₂(x). State the domain, range, and whether the function is increasing or decreasing.
Analyze f(x)=1/x. State its domain, range, and intervals where it is decreasing.
Identify the parent function from its equation and one defining attribute.

optionRationales.cube root: ∛x takes the cube root of x: the cube root parent function.
optionRationales.cubic: Cubic is x³, which raises x to the third power; ∛x undoes that.
optionRationales.square root: A square root has no small number on its radical; this one carries a 3.
optionRationales.logarithmic: A logarithm is written log(x); ∛x is a radical.

responses.label: Which is true?
options: domain and range are both all real numbers
responses.answer: domain and range are both all real numbers

optionRationales.domain and range are both all real numbe: Every real number, negative too, has one real cube root, and the outputs cover every real number.
optionRationales.domain is x≥0: That is true of √x; a cube root works for negatives too: ∛(−8) = −2.
optionRationales.range is y≥0: Cube roots of negative numbers are negative, like ∛(−8) = −2.
optionRationales.x=0 is a vertical asymptote: ∛0 = 0 is defined, so the graph passes smoothly through the origin.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=2ˣ and g(x)=log₂(x), identify the matching asymptotes.

optionRationales.y=0: As x goes left, 2ˣ shrinks toward 0 but never reaches it.
optionRationales.x=0: 2ˣ is defined at x = 0 (2⁰ = 1), so there is no vertical break there.
optionRationales.y=1: y = 1 is where the graph crosses the y-axis, at (0, 1), not a line it approaches.

optionRationales.x=0: log₂(x) needs x > 0 and drops without bound as x nears 0.
optionRationales.y=0: y = 0 belongs to 2ˣ; log₂(x) is its inverse, so x and y trade roles.
optionRationales.x=1: x = 1 is where log₂(x) crosses the x-axis, since log₂(1) = 0, not a line it approaches.
